Subject: Renewal uplift + mid-contract add-on — need invoice path options

Hi Hannah / Marissa,

Thanks again for the QBR yesterday. We have two asks that we need to resolve before our renewal committee meets next week:

1) The clinical team wants to add an extra 40% capacity for throughput during Q3 (estimated 40% uplift to committed tokens) — we need pricing and whether that can be treated as a "mid-contract add" or if it will renew our annual commitment. 
2) Our finance team requires split invoicing for the uplift: 60% billed now (prorated to the remainder of the contract), 40% to be invoiced at renewal. Alternatively, they will accept a single pro-rated invoice if you can provide a short PO amendment template.

Can you share concrete numbers (monthly vs annualized unit price), preferred billing paths, and any constraints around co-terming? Also attaching the updated SOW with technical scope to confirm the sizing.

Thanks,
-Clara

Attachments: ClearPath_SOW_v2.pdf (application/pdf)
message_2:
From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
To: Clara Ruiz <clara.ruiz@clearpath.health>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal uplift + mid-contract add-on — need invoice path options

Clara — thanks for the clear note and the SOW. We can support both paths you described; below are two concrete options and their tradeoffs:

Option A — Prorated single invoice (fastest)
- We prorate the 40% uplift across the remaining contract term; one invoice issued within 7 business days.
- Discount: uplift billed at current committed unit pricing (no additional uplift discount). This preserves your renewal economics and is simplest for PO processing.
- Pros: simplest for finance; quick to bill
- Cons: no financing flexibility; one-time cash impact

Option B — Split billing (finance-friendly)
- 60% of uplift cost invoiced now (prorated to the term), 40% invoiced on renewal date as a "carryforward credit" applied against next term invoice.
- Discount: we can provide a 5% uplift discount on the 40% deferred portion if you commit to the same or higher capacity at renewal (helps offset timing).
- Pros: spreads cash impact; keeps renewal conversation anchored
- Cons: requires amendment to contract (we can template it); accounting will need a credit note flow

Other notes:
- Co-terming: adding capacity mid-contract will not auto-extend your renewal date. You can annualize the uplift at renewal to simplify billing and tax treatment; if you prefer annualization we can convert the 40% uplift to an annualized bucket with tiered pricing — I can share numbers.
- PO template and amendment: attaching a short amendment template and a spreadsheet with example calculations for both options.

I asked Ben to include the sample invoice calculations in the next message. If you have a preferred path, we can draft the Amendment + PO-ready docs and aim to get it signed before your committee next Thursday.

Best,
Hannah

Attachments: price_paths_for_CPH.xlsx (spreadsheet)

P.S. keeping Marissa and Ben in the thread in case we need credit approvals or billing team engagement.

We can issue the prorated invoice using your PO number today if you approve. For the split path we'll prepare the Amendment + credit note language — that will take ~2 business days for legal.

Marissa, can you confirm whether a 5% deferred discount needs additional approvals from revenue ops? If yes, I'll queue it.

Thanks,
Ben
